properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued November 12 at 5:06PM EST until November 12 at 6:00PM EST by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
SVRPHI

The National Weather Service in Mount Holly NJ has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northern Ocean County in southern New Jersey...
Southeastern Monmouth County in central New Jersey...

* Until 600 PM EST.

* At 505 PM EST, severe thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from near East Freehold to near Freewood Acres to
Lakewood to Whiting to near Presidential Lakes Estates, moving
east at 20 mph. This line of storms has a history of producing
hail.

HAZARD...Quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Minor damage to vehicles is possible.

* Locations impacted include...
Toms River, Long Branch, Asbury Park, Lakewood, Jackson, Howell,
Tinton Falls, Beachwood, Manasquan, Point Pleasant Beach, Seaside
Heights, Lakehurst, Farmingdale, Mantoloking, Allenwood, Elberon,
Brick Township, Collingwood Park, Whiting, and Pine Ridge At
Crestwood.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 195 in New Jersey between mile markers 25 and 34.
Garden State Parkway between mile markers 78 and 107.
properties.instruction:
A Tornado Watch remains in effect until 700 PM EST for southern and
central New Jersey.

For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

In addition to large hail, frequent cloud to ground lightning is
occurring with these storms. Move indoors immediately. Remember, if
you can hear thunder, you are close enough to be struck by lightning.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 12 at 1:54PM PST by NWS Spokane WA
properties.description:
* What...Air Quality Advisory because of degraded air quality due to
wildfire smoke. Air Quality Index is forecast to be Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups

* Where...Shoshone and Bonner Counties

* When...Until 11 AM PST Nov 13th

* Impacts...Members of sensitive groups may experience health
effects. The general public is less likely to be affected.
properties.instruction:
Air pollutants can cause breathing difficulties for children, the
elderly, as well as persons with respiratory problems. Those
individuals who are sensitive to increased particulate matter or
smoke are encouraged to avoid prolonged or strenuous outdoor activity
during this advisory. Open burning is prohibited by air quality rule.
It is also recommended that all other individuals limit prolonged or
strenuous activity outdoors.

This statement is updated by the Idaho Department of Environmental
Quality, Air Quality Group. For more information contact DEQ's Coeur
d'Alene Regional Office at 208-769-1422.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

drainage and low-lying areas.

Park.

properties.areaDesc: Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 12 at 12:43PM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves 30 to 35 feet.

* WHERE...Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From 4 PM Friday to 4 AM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and
docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-threatening surf
conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...After only brief improvement late
Saturday through Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late
Sunday through Monday.
properties.instruction:
Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

properties.areaDesc: Guam; Rota; Tinian; Saipan
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 13 at 5:59AM ChST until November 14 at 4:00AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 7 to 10 feet expected in the surf
zone. Dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...North facing reefs of the Marianas.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 AM ChST Saturday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An elevated, long-period north swell is
producing hazardous surf up to 9 feet and a high risk of rip
currents along north-facing reefs. Observation sites have reported
surf up to 7 feet with frequent, larger sets of 7 to 9 feet already
occurring along some north-facing reefs. Swimming conditions will
be dangerous at least through late tonight before surf falls below
hazardous levels of 9 feet shortly afterwards.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents will be life threatening. Inexperienced swimmers
should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions.

If caught in a rip current, relax and float. Don't swim against
the current. If able, swim in a direction following the shoreline.
If unable to escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

and breaking waves due to elevated surf. For the High Surf
Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 7 feet Friday, increasing

to 6 to 9 feet Sunday through Tuesday.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Surf will
we highest for west-northwest facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday
afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from 2 PM Friday to 3
PM PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west-northwesterly
swells are expected to produce large surf into next week with
highest surf and greatest impacts likely peaking Saturday and
potentially again Monday. There is potential for moderate
coastal flooding impacts at times, especially Saturday. Some of
these impacts may be moderate to significant beach erosion and
shallow flooding of normal dry beaches and walkways.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 12 at 11:49AM PST until November 13 at 9:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to
15 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf Warning,
dangerously large breaking waves of 18 to 25 feet with dangerous
rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches. Surf will we highest for west-
northwest facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For
the High Surf Warning, from 9 PM Friday to 3 AM PST Sunday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 3 AM to 6 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...There is a high risk for flooding of sea water over
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide. This includes significant flooding of coastal
beaches, walkways and roads, and potentially damaging some
structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful
waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of
ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers and
jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Remain
far away from the water's edge.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells will
create an extended period of large surf into next week, with the
potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday night through
Monday. Areas that may see most significant impacts will be
west-northwest facing beaches, with widespread flooding likely
at Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo
Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.
properties.instruction:
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other water side
infrastructure.

waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of

jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Remain
far away from the water's edge.

potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday night through

at Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo
Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 12 at 1:20PM CST until November 13 at 9:00AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Los Olmos Creek Near Falfurrias affecting Brooks County.

.The river gauge at Los Olmos Creek near Falfurrias continues to fall
steadily this afternoon, and is now expected to drop below action
stage early Friday morning. The latest forecast has gauge levels
falling well below bankfull over the weekend, and remaining so into
early next week.

For the Los Olmos Creek...including Falfurrias...elevated river
levels are forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues along
the creek banks.

* WHERE...Los Olmos Creek near Falfurrias.

* WHEN...Until Friday morning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 12:15 PM CST Thursday the stage was 6.85 feet and falling.
- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.
- The level has fallen from 8.7 feet at 5 PM Wednesday to below 7
feet just before noon Thursday.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall to 2.1 feet early
Tuesday afternoon, November 17th.
- Action stage is 5.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Additional information is available at www.water.noaa.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 130 AM CST.

properties.areaDesc: Tillamook County Coast
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 12 at 10:22AM PST until November 14 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, tidal overflow flooding
expected. For the High Surf Warning, large waves and dangerous
surf conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet.

* WHERE...Tillamook County Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from noon to 4 PM PST
Friday. For the High Surf Warning, from noon Friday to noon
PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding, up to one foot above ground level,
during high tides is expected in the low lying areas near bays,
sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers.
Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other
structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and
jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe beach
erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings. Higher
than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low- lying
shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave
threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night. In addition,
the Garibaldi tidal gauge is forecast to reach approximately
10.5 ft during high tide Friday afternoon. This typically
results in flooding over Burton-Fraser Rd. along the Tillamook
River.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that tidal overflow flooding is
expected. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

A High Surf Warning means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can lift or roll logs which can injure or kill someone
caught in their path.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 12 at 11:46AM CST by NWS Jackson MS
properties.description:
Recent dry conditions have made outdoor burning increasingly
hazardous. Conditions are such that a spark from equipment, the
heat from a catalytic converter, or any heat source could start a
grass or brush fire. The combination of dry fine fuels, such as
grass, and low relative humidity have resulted in continued fire
danger across the region.

Minimum relative humidity values will range from 25 to 35 percent
this afternoon, creating high fire danger given the dry and breezy
conditions.

Most area counties and parishes are under local burn bans at the
present time. Fires place local forestry agencies, fire
departments, and other fire control agencies in life threatening
situations, and can endanger communities. Please use caution and
help prevent forest and grass fires.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides.

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the Sacramento River, San Joaquin
River, and other Delta waterways in Solano, Yolo, Sacramento, and
San Joaquin Counties.

* WHEN...Until 400 PM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 930 AM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that
abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.
- The highest tides forecast each day are (all times local
time):
* Port Chicago: 1.2 ft above normal (6.1 ft MLLW) at 2:15 PM
Thu 11/12, 1.0 ft above normal (5.9 ft MLLW) at 2:56 PM Fri
11/13, 0.7 ft above normal (5.6 ft MLLW) at 3:44 PM Sat
11/14, and 0.3 ft above normal (5.2 ft MLLW) at 4:39 PM Sun
11/15.
* West Sacramento: 1.2 ft above normal (5.5 ft MLLW) at 5:28
PM Thu 11/12, 1.0 ft above normal (5.4 ft MLLW) at 6:10 PM
Fri 11/13, 0.9 ft above normal (5.2 ft MLLW) at 6:57 PM Sat
11/14, and 0.6 ft above normal (5.0 ft MLLW) at 7:50 PM Sun
11/15.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.5 ft at 5:00 PM Thu 11/12,
+7.7 ft at 5:00 PM Fri 11/13, and +7.6 ft at 6:00 PM Sat
11/14.
- These predictions include up to +1.1 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary up to an hour throughout the San
Francisco Bay and Delta.
- Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at:
* Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre
dictions.html?id=9415144
* West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide
predictions.html?id=9416131

properties.instruction:

tide. If you encounter flooded roadways: turn around, dont drown.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 12 at 12:33PM EST until November 13 at 12:00PM EST by NWS Marquette MI
properties.description:
...ACCUMULATING LAKE EFFECT SNOW CONTINUES THROUGH FRIDAY...

.Lake effect snow showers will continue through Friday. Wet snow
accumulations are expected away from the Lake Superior shoreline with
several inches of snowfall over the higher terrain.

* WHAT...Lake effect snow. Additional snow accumulations between 3
and 7 inches over the higher elevations of Marquette and Baraga
Counties with up to 10 inches in rural areas north of US-41 and
west of Marquette County Road 510. Less than an inch of snow is
expected near Lake Superior. Winds gusting as high as 25 mph and up
to 35 mph near Lake Superior.

* WHERE...Baraga and Marquette Counties.

* WHEN...Until noon EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
will impact the Thursday evening and Friday morning commutes.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Warmer temperatures near Lake Superior will
limit snow accumulations to less than an inch near the lakeshore,
including the city of Marquette. Conditions will deteriorate as you
move inland, particularly US-41 between Marquette and Negaunee.
Snow showers are expected to increase in intensity this afternoon
into tonight.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling.

During lake effect snow, the weather can vary from bands of locally
heavy snow to dry weather just a few miles away. Visibilities can
also vary greatly. Be prepared for rapid changes in weather,
visibility, and road conditions.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 12 at 10:24AM CST by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
Elevated fire weather conditions can be expected across portions
of southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi this afternoon.
Relative humidity values are forecast to drop into the 25 to 35
percent range, especially near and north of the Interstate 10 and
12 corridors. The 20 ft wind forecast is expected to remain at or
below 10 mph in most areas, which should limit critical fire
weather conditions or at least the effective spread of fires that
may ignite.

Numerous local burn bans are in place across LA and MS due to
ongoing drought conditions. Outdoor burning is strongly
discouraged as the ongoing drought conditions continue, and all
local restrictions should be followed.

NWSheadline: ELEVATED FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS THIS AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: South Central Oregon Coast; Curry County Coast
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 12 at 2:29AM PST until November 14 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves of 20 to 25 ft Friday,
increasing to 30 to 35 ft late Friday through Saturday.

* WHERE...Beaches of South Central Oregon Coast and Curry County
Coast. This includes Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and
Brookings.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Friday to 10 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Extremely large breaking waves will create very
hazardous conditions along beaches and area shorelines. Waves
will inundate beaches and surge into normally dry areas.
Infrastructure damage and significant beach erosion can be
expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Conditions may improve somewhat late
Saturday as breaking wave heights lower to 24 to 27 ft, but
another large ocean swell will maintain hazardous beach
conditions much of the weekend and into Monday.

* View the hazard area in detail at
https://www.wrh.noaa.gov/map/?wfo=mfr
properties.instruction:
Beaches and coastlines will become hazardous due to very large
and life-threatening surf conditions. Stay off of beaches, rocks,
jetties,piers, and other waterside infrastructure.

properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 12 at 2:12AM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of northwest Washington, including the following
county, Mason.

* WHEN...From late tonight through late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Three to four and a half inches of rain is forecast for the south
slopes of the Olympics between early Friday and early Sunday with
snow levels of 5500 to 6500 feet. The combination of heavy rain
and relatively high snow levels could push the Skokomish River
near Potlatch above flood stage.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH IN EFFECT FROM LATE TONIGHT THROUGH LATE SATURDAY NIGHT

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 11 at 10:48PM PST until November 13 at 6:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the
High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to 35
ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints.
For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, large breaking waves will
run up beaches and crash over seawalls, inundating adjacent,
low-lying infrastructure.

* WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur
Coast.

* WHEN...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST
Friday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday
afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM Friday to 4 AM
PST Sunday. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, from
midnight Friday night to 6 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the
shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from
beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide
is expected to be: 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 12:10 PM
Thursday 11/12, 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM
Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the
Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea
walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 11 at 10:48PM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the
High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to 35
ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints.
For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, large breaking waves will
run up beaches and crash over seawalls, inundating adjacent,
low-lying infrastructure.

* WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur
Coast.

* WHEN...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST
Friday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday
afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM Friday to 4 AM
PST Sunday. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, from
midnight Friday night to 6 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the
shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from
beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide
is expected to be: 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 12:10 PM
Thursday 11/12, 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM
Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the
Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea
walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.areaDesc: Bonner, ID; Shoshone, ID
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 11 at 4:52PM PST by NWS Spokane WA
properties.description:
* What...Air Quality Advisory because of degraded air quality due to
wildfire smoke. Air Quality Index is forecast to be Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups

* Where...Shoshone and Bonner Counties

* When...Until 11 AM PST Nov 13th

* Impacts...Members of sensitive groups may experience health
effects. The general public is less likely to be affected.
properties.instruction:
Air pollutants can cause breathing difficulties for children, the
elderly, as well as persons with respiratory problems. Those
individuals who are sensitive to increased particulate matter or
smoke are encouraged to avoid prolonged or strenuous outdoor activity
during this advisory. Open burning is prohibited by air quality rule.
It is also recommended that all other individuals limit prolonged or
strenuous activity outdoors.

This statement is updated by the Idaho Department of Environmental
Quality, Air Quality Group. For more information contact DEQ's Coeur
d'Alene Regional Office at 208-769-1422.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

NWSheadline: An Air Quality Advisory has been issued by the Idaho Department of Environmental Quality in Coeur d'Alene for Shoshone and Bonner Counties

properties.areaDesc: Los Angeles County Beaches; Los Angeles County Inland Coast including Downtown Los Angeles
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 11 at 11:29AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has extended an air quality alert due
to harmful levels of fine particle pollution.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...in Vernon, Maywood, Bell Gardens, Westmont, Hawthorne,
Inglewood, Downtown LA, East LA and Huntington Park. Levels of
particle pollution can vary by time and location depending on
emissions and local weather conditions.

* WHEN...until 11:59 PM Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Particle pollution can get deep into the lungs and cause
serious health problems such as heart attacks, bronchitis, asthma
attacks, and difficulty breathing. Everyone can be affected, but
sensitive groups such as people with lung or heart disease, older
adults, people who are pregnant, children, and those who spend a lot
of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.
